title: 2003 AMC 12B Problem 21
statement: An object moves \(8\) cm in a straight line from \(A\) to \(B,\) turns at an angle \(\alpha,\) measured in radians and chosen at random from the interval \((0, \pi),\) and moves \(5\) cm in a straight line to \(C.\) What is the probability that \(AC \lt 7?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(\beta = \pi - \alpha\) be the interior angle of \(\triangle ABC\) at \(B.\) By the Law of Cosines, \[ \begin{aligned} &AC^2 = 8^2 + 5^2 \\ &\quad {}- 2(8)(5)\cos\beta \\ &= 89 - 80\cos\beta. \end{aligned} \]

Then \(AC \lt 7\) means \(89 - 80\cos\beta \lt 49,\) i.e. \(\cos\beta \gt \dfrac{1}{2},\) i.e. \(\beta \lt \dfrac{\pi}{3}.\)

As \(\alpha\) is uniform on \((0, \pi),\) so is \(\beta.\) The probability is \[ \frac{\frac{\pi}{3}}{\pi} = \frac{1}{3}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(\beta = \pi - \alpha\) be the interior angle at \(B;\) apply the Law of Cosines to \(\triangle ABC\)
